findings.evidence: "Only once every condition above is met does the home-office equipment stipend become available to the employee."
findings.fix: Change to "Only when all conditions above are met does the home-office equipment stipend become available to the employee."
findings.violation: The phrasing "once every condition" is ambiguous and likely should be "once all conditions" or "when all conditions."

findings.evidence: "Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email."
findings.fix: Remove this sentence entirely or rewrite it to describe the actual policy process for how the backup reviewer is notified.
findings.location: How to Apply section, final paragraph
findings.violation: This sentence describes a specific operational failure rather than the intended policy process.

findings.evidence: Approval Timeline says "The manager confirms the equipment category matches the approved list." Required Documentation says "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist."
findings.fix: Clarify whether managers must strictly follow the approved list or have discretionary authority, then align both sections.
findings.location: Approval Timeline section vs. Required Documentation section
findings.violation: These statements contradict each other - one requires managers to verify compliance with the approved list, the other grants them discretion to approve items outside the checklist.

findings.evidence: "Also, the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time."
findings.fix: Change to "Also, the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee has already paid."
findings.violation: The phrase "at this point in time" is redundant since reimbursement inherently occurs after costs have already been incurred.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Change to "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and may be asked for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, first sentence
findings.violation: The sentence shifts inconsistently between second person ("you") and first person plural ("we").

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, second sentence
findings.violation: "Similarly" does not logically connect this statement to the preceding sentence about equipment maintenance and photo checks.

findings.evidence: "Program Overview" states "The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter." The later "Overview" section states "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period."
findings.fix: Merge these two sections into one consistent "Overview" and reconcile the conflicting statements about publication responsibility and schedule.
findings.location: Document structure - two separate sections titled "Program Overview" and "Overview"
findings.violation: The document contains duplicate section headers with conflicting information about which team publishes the log and at what frequency (quarterly vs. after enrollment).

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Either expand this section to list all steps or clarify that eligibility confirmation and receipt upload are the only required steps.
findings.violation: This section lists only two steps, but the How to Apply section describes the portal walking "through each step in order," implying a multi-step process.
